### 目标

### 论文 Framing（paper_framing.md 摘要）
**标题方向**: B-IAVR: Selective Self-Verification via RL
**Core Insight**: 大多数 self-verification 是 confirmatory 而非 corrective。用 action change 作为 reward signal，RL 训练 agent 只在 verification 真正 informative 时触发，实现 cost-efficiency。
**Story**: Cost-efficiency，不走 performance。

**Core Claims**:
1. Selective verification reduces cost while preserving performance
2. Action change 是有效的 verification informativeness reward
3. Learned policy > heuristic baselines

**竞争者差异化**:
| 维度 | ARES | B-IAVR |
|------|------|--------|
| Decision | Continuous effort allocation | Binary verify/skip |
| Training | SFT on filtered data → GRPO | RL (GRPO) with action-change reward |
| Signal | Pre-defined quality metrics | Behavioral change (action change) |
| Scope | Reasoning tasks | Interactive agent tasks |

**D041 更新**: GiGPO (step-level credit assignment) 已确认为 Plan D 首选路线。GiGPO 的嵌套组结构提供 step-level dense reward signal，与当前 binary sparse reward 互补。Method section 应预留 GiGPO 集成的描述空间。

### 需要包含的内容

#### 3.1 Problem Formulation
- Interactive agent 任务建模为 POMDP / MDP
- Verification decision 形式化：每步 binary decision $d_t \in \{0, 1\}$（verify / skip）
- Action-change signal 定义：$\Delta a_t = \mathbb{1}[a_t^{\text{post-verify}} \neq a_t^{\text{pre-verify}}]$
- Verification cost model：$C_{\text{total}} = \sum_{t} d_t \cdot c_{\text{verify}}$
- 目标函数：maximize task success while minimizing verification cost

#### 3.2 B-IAVR Method
- **Selective Verification Policy**: 策略 $\pi_\theta(d_t | s_t)$ 决定何时触发 verification
- **Reward Design**: 
  - Task success reward: $r_{\text{task}}$ (binary, episode-level)
  - Action-change reward: $r_{\text{ac}} = \alpha \cdot \Delta a_t$ (step-level, verification informativeness proxy)
  - Combined: $R = r_{\text{task}} + \beta \cdot \sum_t d_t \cdot r_{\text{ac},t} - \gamma \cdot C_{\text{total}}$
- **Training**: GRPO / GiGPO (预留两种描述)
  - GRPO baseline: episode-level advantage
  - GiGPO extension: step-level credit assignment via nested groups
- **Self-Guide Integration**: co-evolving internal reward 作为 verification trigger signal

#### 3.3 Comparison with Related Methods
- vs ARES: binary decision vs continuous allocation; action-change vs token efficiency; no annotated data needed
- vs Thinkless: interactive agents vs single-turn reasoning; environment-grounded signal vs token-level control
- vs Derailer-Rerailer: RL-trained vs heuristic; multi-turn agent vs reasoning chain

# Generated: 2026-05-15
# Updated: 2026-05-15 (D041: Plan D GiGPO/step-level credit added as P0)
# Based on: paper_framing.md (D039), ROADMAP.md, registry data
#
# Phases:
#   A — Always-on Self-Guidance baseline (prerequisite for all claims)
#   B — B-IAVR selective verification training
#   C — Ablation matrix & causal analysis
#   D — ARES baseline comparison
#   E — GiGPO / step-level credit assignment (D041 Plan D, P0 备选路线)
#
# GPU budget: 2× RTX PRO 6000 96GB (cuda:0, cuda:1) @ bjb1-17606
# Total estimate: ~1100-1700 GPU-h

experiments:

  # ============================================================
  # Phase A: Always-On Self-Guidance Baseline
  # ============================================================

  - plan_id: "plan_001"
    title: "Stabilized GRPO always-on baseline (exp027)"
    claim: "Claim 1"
    phase: "A"
    priority: "P0"
    depends_on: []
    registry_id: "exp027_stable_grpo"
    status: "running"
    description: >
      128 rollouts + entropy 0.01 + LR 5e-7 + KL 0.005 GRPO training
      on Qwen3-1.7B with always-on self-verification in ALFWorld.
      50 steps, dual-GPU. Fixes exp026 death spiral via larger rollout
      buffer and conservative hyperparams.
      Early stop (D041): step 10 train success ≤12% → terminate.
    hypothesis: >
      Stabilized GRPO avoids reward collapse and reaches ≥20% success (MVP).
    metrics: ["success_rate", "action_is_valid", "kl_divergence", "entropy"]
    gpu_hours_estimate: 84
    framing_ref: "reviewer_concern_1"
    nine_dim: [1, 3]

  - plan_id: "plan_002"
    title: "Extended GRPO training (100 steps / higher LR)"
    claim: "Claim 1"
    phase: "A"
    priority: "P0"
    depends_on: ["plan_001"]
    registry_id: null
    status: "planned"
    description: >
      If exp027 reaches 20-30% but not 50%, extend training: either continue
      from best checkpoint with 50 more steps, or restart with higher LR
      (1e-6) and/or larger rollout buffer (256). Target: success ≥50% for
      credible cost-efficiency story.
    hypothesis: >
      Longer training or modestly higher LR pushes baseline past 50% threshold
      needed for paper's cost-efficiency claim.
    metrics: ["success_rate", "action_is_valid", "kl_divergence"]
    gpu_hours_estimate: 168
    framing_ref: "reviewer_concern_1"
    nine_dim: [1, 5]

  - plan_id: "plan_003"
    title: "Multi-seed baseline replication (3 seeds)"
    claim: "Claim 1"
    phase: "A"
    priority: "P1"
    depends_on: ["plan_002"]
    registry_id: null
    status: "planned"
    description: >
      Replicate best Phase A config across 3 random seeds to report
      mean ± std success rate. Required for statistical credibility
      of all downstream comparisons.
    hypothesis: >
      Baseline success rate is reproducible (std < 5pp across seeds).
    metrics: ["success_rate_mean", "success_rate_std"]
    gpu_hours_estimate: 252
    framing_ref: null
    nine_dim: [3]

  # ============================================================
  # Phase B: B-IAVR Selective Verification
  # ============================================================

  - plan_id: "plan_004"
    title: "Action-change reward signal analysis"
    claim: "Claim 2"
    phase: "B"
    priority: "P0"
    depends_on: ["plan_001"]
    registry_id: null
    status: "planned"
    description: >
      Before training B-IAVR policy, collect action-change statistics from
      Phase A always-on runs: (1) what fraction of verifications trigger
      action change, (2) correlation between action change and episode
      success, (3) per-task-type breakdown. This informs reward design
      and provides empirical grounding for Claim 2.
    hypothesis: >
      Action change after verification positively correlates with episode
      success (r > 0.2), and most verifications are confirmatory (>60%
      produce no action change).
    metrics: ["action_change_rate", "action_change_success_correlation", "confirmatory_rate"]
    gpu_hours_estimate: 4
    framing_ref: "reviewer_concern_3"
    nine_dim: [1, 4]

  - plan_id: "plan_005"
    title: "B-IAVR binary verify/skip policy (GRPO)"
    claim: "Claim 1"
    phase: "B"
    priority: "P0"
    depends_on: ["plan_002", "plan_004"]
    registry_id: null
    status: "planned"
    description: >
      Train selective verification policy via GRPO. Agent learns a binary
      decision (verify / skip) at each step. Reward = task_success +
      alpha * action_change_when_verified - beta * verification_cost.
      Initialize from Phase A best checkpoint. Action-change component
      encourages verification only when it would change the agent's action.
    hypothesis: >
      B-IAVR achieves verification rate ↓40%+ compared to always-on
      while maintaining success within 5pp of baseline.
    metrics: ["success_rate", "verification_rate", "cost_reduction", "action_change_rate"]
    gpu_hours_estimate: 168
    framing_ref: "reviewer_concern_1"
    nine_dim: [1, 4]

  - plan_id: "plan_006"
    title: "B-IAVR multi-seed replication (3 seeds)"
    claim: "Claim 1"
    phase: "B"
    priority: "P1"
    depends_on: ["plan_005"]
    registry_id: null
    status: "planned"
    description: >
      Replicate best B-IAVR config across 3 seeds. Report mean ± std for
      success rate, verification rate, and cost reduction.
    hypothesis: >
      B-IAVR cost reduction is reproducible (std < 5pp across seeds).
    metrics: ["success_rate_mean", "success_rate_std", "verification_rate_mean", "cost_reduction_mean"]
    gpu_hours_estimate: 252
    framing_ref: null
    nine_dim: [3]

  # ============================================================
  # Phase C: Ablation Matrix & Causal Analysis
  # ============================================================

  - plan_id: "plan_007"
    title: "No-verify ablation"
    claim: "Claim 3"
    phase: "C"
    priority: "P0"
    depends_on: ["plan_002"]
    registry_id: null
    status: "planned"
    description: >
      Train agent with verification completely disabled. Same GRPO config
      as Phase A but no self-verification step. Lower bound for ablation
      matrix — demonstrates verification value.
    hypothesis: >
      Removing verification drops success by ≥10pp vs always-on baseline,
      confirming verification contributes to task performance.
    metrics: ["success_rate", "action_is_valid"]
    gpu_hours_estimate: 84
    framing_ref: null
    nine_dim: [4]

  - plan_id: "plan_008"
    title: "Random-p verification ablation (p=0.3, 0.5, 0.7)"
    claim: "Claim 3"
    phase: "C"
    priority: "P0"
    depends_on: ["plan_002"]
    registry_id: null
    status: "planned"
    description: >
      Verify at random with probability p ∈ {0.3, 0.5, 0.7}. No learning —
      just stochastic verification on top of Phase A checkpoint. Heuristic
      baseline for Claim 3 (learned > heuristic).
    hypothesis: >
      Random verification underperforms B-IAVR at same verification budget:
      either lower success or higher verification rate for same success.
    metrics: ["success_rate", "verification_rate", "cost_reduction"]
    gpu_hours_estimate: 6
    framing_ref: null
    nine_dim: [2, 4]

  - plan_id: "plan_009"
    title: "Confidence-threshold verification ablation"
    claim: "Claim 3"
    phase: "C"
    priority: "P0"
    depends_on: ["plan_002"]
    registry_id: null
    status: "planned"
    description: >
      Verify only when model's next-token entropy exceeds threshold τ.
      Sweep τ ∈ {0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0}. Heuristic baseline representing
      "verify when uncertain" strategy.
    hypothesis: >
      Confidence-threshold achieves some cost reduction but is suboptimal
      vs learned B-IAVR policy because entropy doesn't capture verification
      informativeness.
    metrics: ["success_rate", "verification_rate", "cost_reduction"]
    gpu_hours_estimate: 8
    framing_ref: null
    nine_dim: [2, 4]

  - plan_id: "plan_010"
    title: "Entropy-controlled action-change analysis"
    claim: "Claim 2"
    phase: "C"
    priority: "P0"
    depends_on: ["plan_004"]
    registry_id: null
    status: "planned"
    description: >
      Key defense for Reviewer Concern 3 (action change = noise vs signal).
      Stratify episodes by policy entropy. Within each entropy stratum,
      test whether action change after verification still correlates with
      task success. If correlation holds after controlling for entropy,
      action change reflects genuine informativeness, not random noise
      from high-entropy policies.
    hypothesis: >
      Partial correlation between action change and success remains
      significant (p < 0.05) after controlling for policy entropy.
    metrics: ["partial_correlation", "p_value", "per_stratum_effect_size"]
    gpu_hours_estimate: 4
    framing_ref: "reviewer_concern_3"
    nine_dim: [4]

  - plan_id: "plan_011"
    title: "Causal intervention: random vs verification-triggered action change"
    claim: "Claim 2"
    phase: "C"
    priority: "P0"
    depends_on: ["plan_002"]
    registry_id: null
    status: "planned"
    description: >
      Causal experiment for Reviewer Concern 3. Two conditions on Phase A
      checkpoint: (1) inject random action changes at same rate as
      verification-triggered changes, (2) allow only verification-triggered
      changes. Compare task success between conditions. If (2) >> (1),
      verification-triggered changes have causal efficacy beyond noise.
    hypothesis: >
      Verification-triggered action changes yield ≥10pp higher success
      than random action changes at same change rate.
    metrics: ["success_rate_verification_triggered", "success_rate_random_change", "delta"]
    gpu_hours_estimate: 8
    framing_ref: "reviewer_concern_3"
    nine_dim: [4]

  - plan_id: "plan_012"
    title: "Reward signal comparison: action-change vs random-trigger vs confidence"
    claim: "Claim 2"
    phase: "C"
    priority: "P1"
    depends_on: ["plan_005"]
    registry_id: null
    status: "planned"
    description: >
      Train B-IAVR with 3 alternative reward signals: (a) action-change
      (ours), (b) random trigger reward, (c) confidence-based reward.
      Same GRPO setup, same budget. Demonstrates action-change is the
      best verification informativeness signal.
    hypothesis: >
      Action-change reward produces best cost-performance tradeoff
      (highest success at lowest verification rate).
    metrics: ["success_rate", "verification_rate", "cost_reduction", "training_convergence_step"]
    gpu_hours_estimate: 336
    framing_ref: "reviewer_concern_3"
    nine_dim: [4, 5]

  - plan_id: "plan_013"
    title: "Verification cost weight sensitivity (alpha/beta sweep)"
    claim: "Claim 1"
    phase: "C"
    priority: "P2"
    depends_on: ["plan_005"]
    registry_id: null
    status: "planned"
    description: >
      Sweep alpha (action-change weight) and beta (verification cost
      weight) in B-IAVR reward: alpha ∈ {0.1, 0.3, 0.5}, beta ∈
      {0.01, 0.05, 0.1}. 9 configs, short training (20 steps each).
      Maps the cost-performance Pareto frontier.
    hypothesis: >
      Pareto frontier shows smooth tradeoff; optimal beta ≈ 0.05
      achieves ≥40% cost reduction with <3pp success drop.
    metrics: ["success_rate", "verification_rate", "cost_reduction"]
    gpu_hours_estimate: 120
    framing_ref: null
    nine_dim: [5]

  # ============================================================
  # Phase D: ARES Baseline Comparison
  # ============================================================

  - plan_id: "plan_014"
    title: "ARES reproduction on ALFWorld (SFT router)"
    claim: "Claim 3"
    phase: "D"
    priority: "P1"
    depends_on: ["plan_002"]
    registry_id: null
    status: "planned"
    description: >
      Reproduce ARES (arXiv 2603.07915) approach on ALFWorld: train
      SFT-based router that allocates verification effort based on
      pre-defined quality metrics. Adapt their continuous effort
      allocation to our binary verify/skip for fair comparison.
      Use same base model (Qwen3-1.7B) and training data.
    hypothesis: >
      ARES SFT router achieves moderate cost reduction but with
      lower ceiling than RL-based B-IAVR because SFT cannot explore
      beyond training distribution.
    metrics: ["success_rate", "verification_rate", "cost_reduction"]
    gpu_hours_estimate: 24
    framing_ref: "reviewer_concern_5"
    nine_dim: [2]

  - plan_id: "plan_015"
    title: "B-IAVR vs ARES head-to-head comparison"
    claim: "Claim 3"
    phase: "D"
    priority: "P1"
    depends_on: ["plan_005", "plan_014"]
    registry_id: null
    status: "planned"
    description: >
      Controlled comparison: B-IAVR (RL, action-change reward) vs
      ARES (SFT, quality metrics) on identical eval episodes.
      Report success rate, verification rate, cost reduction, and
      per-task-type breakdown. Addresses Reviewer Concern 5
      (ARES differentiation).
    hypothesis: >
      B-IAVR achieves ≥10pp better cost reduction than ARES at
      matched success level, due to RL exploration advantage and
      action-change signal superiority.
    metrics: ["success_rate", "verification_rate", "cost_reduction", "per_task_type_breakdown"]
    gpu_hours_estimate: 4
    framing_ref: "reviewer_concern_5"
    nine_dim: [2, 4]

  # Phase E: GiGPO / Step-Level Credit Assignment (D041 Plan D)
  # ============================================================
  # D041 战略更新：sparse binary reward 是 exp027 的根本瓶颈，
  # GiGPO/step-level credit 是打破 10% plateau 的首选备选路线。
  # Self-Guide 同模型(Qwen3-1.7B)同环境(ALFWorld)达 72.7%，
  # 关键差异是 step-level dense reward vs binary sparse reward。

  - plan_id: "plan_018"
    title: "GiGPO / step-level credit feasibility & implementation"
    claim: "Claim 1"
    phase: "E"
    priority: "P0"
    depends_on: []
    registry_id: null
    status: "planned"
    description: >
      D041 首选备选路线。评估并实现 GiGPO (arXiv 2505.10978) 或
      Self-Guide (arXiv 2604.03098) 的 step-level credit assignment
      在 RAGEN/verl 框架中的集成。三个候选方案：
      (A) GiGPO 嵌套组结构 — step-level credit 无需 learned critic
      (B) Self-Guide co-evolving internal reward — 每步 dense reward
      (C) Heuristic step reward (action_is_valid + progress signal)
      选择改动量最小、与现有 pipeline 兼容性最好的方案。
    hypothesis: >
      Step-level credit assignment 解决 sparse reward 学习信号密度不足，
      打破 10% success plateau。
    metrics: ["implementation_loc", "integration_complexity", "compatibility"]
    gpu_hours_estimate: 8
    framing_ref: "reviewer_concern_1"
    nine_dim: [4]

  - plan_id: "plan_019"
    title: "Step-level credit GRPO training (Phase A replacement)"
    claim: "Claim 1"
    phase: "E"
    priority: "P0"
    depends_on: ["plan_018"]
    registry_id: null
    status: "planned"
    description: >
      用 plan_018 选定的 step-level credit 方案替换 binary sparse reward，
      重新训练 always-on baseline。从 exp021 SFT checkpoint 出发，
      GRPO + step-level reward，50-100 steps。目标：success ≥50%
      (Self-Guide 同配置达 72.7%)。如成功，此实验替代 plan_001/002
      成为 Phase B 的起点。
    hypothesis: >
      Step-level dense reward 使 GRPO 训练突破 10% plateau，
      达到 50%+ success，为 cost-efficiency story 提供足够强的 baseline。
    metrics: ["success_rate", "action_is_valid", "step_reward_density", "kl_divergence"]
    gpu_hours_estimate: 84
    framing_ref: "reviewer_concern_1"
    nine_dim: [1]

  - plan_id: "plan_020"
    title: "Self-Guide reward reproduction & ablation"
    claim: "Claim 2"
    phase: "E"
    priority: "P0"
    depends_on: ["plan_018"]
    registry_id: null
    status: "planned"
    description: >
      复现 Self-Guide (arXiv 2604.03098) 的 co-evolving internal reward
      在 ALFWorld 上的结果。验证 72.7% success 是否可复现。
      同时做 reward ablation：(a) Self-Guide full reward, (b) env-only
      sparse reward, (c) heuristic step reward。确认 Self-Guide reward
      是 performance 提升的关键因素。
    hypothesis: >
      Self-Guide reward 复现达 60%+ success (论文报告 72.7%)，
      显著优于 sparse-only baseline。
    metrics: ["success_rate", "reward_density", "convergence_speed"]
    gpu_hours_estimate: 168
    framing_ref: null
    nine_dim: [1, 2, 4]

  # ============================================================
  # Auxiliary Analyses
  # ============================================================

  - plan_id: "plan_016"
    title: "Per-task-type performance breakdown"
    claim: "Claim 1"
    phase: "A"
    priority: "P1"
    depends_on: ["plan_002"]
    registry_id: null
    status: "planned"
    description: >
      Breakdown always-on baseline and B-IAVR results by ALFWorld
      task type (pick, clean, heat, cool, examine, pick_two).
      Identifies where verification helps most and addresses
      Reviewer Concern 2 (single environment) by showing within-
      environment diversity.
    hypothesis: >
      Verification benefit varies across task types; manipulation-
      heavy tasks (pick_two, clean) benefit most from verification.
    metrics: ["per_task_success", "per_task_verification_benefit"]
    gpu_hours_estimate: 2
    framing_ref: "reviewer_concern_2"
    nine_dim: [1]

  - plan_id: "plan_017"
    title: "Scale analysis: model size framing"
    claim: "Claim 1"
    phase: "C"
    priority: "P2"
    depends_on: ["plan_005"]
    registry_id: null
    status: "planned"
    description: >
      Analytical defense for Reviewer Concern 4 (small model).
      Compare verification patterns at 1.7B: how often does the
      model "need" verification (action change rate), and how does
      this relate to model uncertainty? Frame 1.7B as the regime
      where selective verification is most valuable (weaker models
      have more room for improvement from verification, but also
      more noise — B-IAVR navigates this tradeoff).
    hypothesis: >
      1.7B model has high confirmatory verification rate (>60%),
      making selective verification especially cost-effective at
      this scale.
    metrics: ["confirmatory_rate", "action_change_rate", "model_uncertainty"]
    gpu_hours_estimate: 2
    framing_ref: "reviewer_concern_4"
    nine_dim: [1, 4]

## 任务：Method Section 初稿骨架

### 目标
在 `artifacts/docs/method_draft.md` 写 Method section 初稿骨架。用 register_artifact 注册产出。

### 论文 framing 上下文

**项目**: B-IAVR (Behaviorally-grounded Interactive Agent Verification via RL)
**核心 insight**: 大多数 self-verification 是 confirmatory 而非 corrective。用 action change 作为 reward signal，RL 训练 agent 只在 verification 真正 informative 时触发验证，实现 cost-efficiency。
**Story arc**: Cost-efficiency story，不走 performance story。

**Core Claims:**
1. Selective verification reduces cost while preserving performance
2. Action change 是有效的 verification informativeness reward
3. Learned policy > heuristic baselines

**竞争者差异化（vs ARES）:**
- ARES: continuous effort allocation, SFT router, pre-defined quality metrics, reasoning tasks
- B-IAVR: binary verify/skip, RL (GRPO), action-change signal, interactive agent tasks

**vs Thinkless:**
- Thinkless: RL-trained control token for reasoning thinking mode
- B-IAVR: RL-trained verification decision for interactive agent trajectories

### 技术细节

**环境**: ALFWorld (text-based household tasks, 6 task types: pick, clean, heat, cool, examine, pick_two)
**模型**: Qwen3-1.7B (instruct)
**训练框架**: RAGEN (基于 verl) + GRPO
**Self-Guide baseline**: arXiv 2604.03098, always-on verification, co-evolving internal reward, 72.7% on ALFWorld 1.7B

**B-IAVR 方法核心**:
1. Agent 在每个 step 做 binary decision: verify (触发 self-verification) 或 skip (直接执行)
2. Verification = 重新观察环境状态 → 判断当前计划的 action 是否需要修改
3. Action-change signal: 如果 verification 导致 agent 改变了原计划的 action → 说明 verification 是 informative 的
4. Reward design: task_success + alpha * action_change_when_verified - beta * verification_cost
5. 训练: GRPO with binary verify/skip as additional action dimension

**GiGPO (备选 D041)**: Group-in-Group Policy Optimization, 嵌套组结构提供 step-level credit assignment, >12% over GRPO on ALFWorld

### 骨架结构要求

```markdown
## 3. Method

### 3.1 Problem Formulation
- Interactive agent as POMDP
- Verification decision formalization
- Action-change signal 数学定义
[数学符号定义清晰]

### 3.2 B-IAVR: Selective Verification Policy
- Policy architecture (binary decision head)
- Verification mechanism
- Action-change detection

### 3.3 Training with Action-Change Reward
- Reward design (task_success + action_change + verification_cost)
- GRPO training procedure
- 与 ARES/Thinkless 的方法论对比

### 3.4 Implementation Details
- Model, environment, hyperparameters
[留 TBD 占位符给实验结果]
```

### 写作规范
- 数学符号定义清晰一致（state s_t, action a_t, verification decision v_t ∈ {0,1}）
- 留 `[TBD: exp result]` 占位符（不依赖 exp027 结果）
- 与竞争者对比要公平客观
- 不做 performance claim（当前无数据支撑）
- 用 LaTeX 数学符号（$...$）
- 中英文混合可，以清晰为主

### 输出
写到 `artifacts/docs/method_draft.md`，用 register_artifact 注册。

# Experiment Plan — B-IAVR: Selective Self-Verification via RL
# Generated: 2026-05-15 | Updated: 2026-05-15 (D041: Plan D GiGPO added)
# Based on: paper_framing.md (D039), ROADMAP.md, registry data, D041 strategic update
#
# Phases:
#   A — Always-on Self-Guidance baseline (prerequisite for all claims)
#   B — B-IAVR selective verification training
#   C — Ablation matrix & causal analysis
#   D — ARES baseline comparison
#
# GPU budget: 2× RTX PRO 6000 96GB (cuda:0, cuda:1) @ bjb1-17606
# Total estimate: ~1000-1600 GPU-h

experiments:

  # ============================================================
  # Phase A: Always-On Self-Guidance Baseline
  # ============================================================

  - plan_id: "plan_001"
    title: "Stabilized GRPO always-on baseline (exp027)"
    claim: "Claim 1"
    phase: "A"
    priority: "P0"
    depends_on: []
    registry_id: "exp027_stable_grpo"
    status: "running"
    description: >
      128 rollouts + entropy 0.01 + LR 5e-7 + KL 0.005 GRPO training
      on Qwen3-1.7B with always-on self-verification in ALFWorld.
      50 steps, dual-GPU. Fixes exp026 death spiral via larger rollout
      buffer and conservative hyperparams. Early stop: step 10 train
      success ≤12% → terminate (D041).
    hypothesis: >
      Stabilized GRPO avoids reward collapse and reaches ≥20% success (MVP).
    metrics: ["success_rate", "action_is_valid", "kl_divergence", "entropy"]
    gpu_hours_estimate: 84
    framing_ref: "reviewer_concern_1"
    nine_dim: [1, 3]

  - plan_id: "plan_002"
    title: "Extended GRPO training (100 steps / higher LR)"
    claim: "Claim 1"
    phase: "A"
    priority: "P0"
    depends_on: ["plan_001"]
    registry_id: null
    status: "planned"
    description: >
      If exp027 reaches 20-30% but not 50%, extend training: either continue
      from best checkpoint with 50 more steps, or restart with higher LR
      (1e-6) and/or larger rollout buffer (256). Target: success ≥50% for
      credible cost-efficiency story.
    hypothesis: >
      Longer training or modestly higher LR pushes baseline past 50% threshold
      needed for paper's cost-efficiency claim.
    metrics: ["success_rate", "action_is_valid", "kl_divergence"]
    gpu_hours_estimate: 168
    framing_ref: "reviewer_concern_1"
    nine_dim: [1, 5]

  - plan_id: "plan_002b"
    title: "GiGPO step-level credit assignment (Phase A fallback / upgrade)"
    claim: "Claim 1"
    phase: "A"
    priority: "P0"
    depends_on: ["plan_001"]
    registry_id: null
    status: "planned"
    description: >
      D041 首选备选路线。GiGPO (arXiv 2505.10978) 引入两级 advantage:
      episode-level (同 GRPO) + step-level (anchor state grouping)。
      解决 exp027 的核心瓶颈: sparse binary reward 下 4/8 groups 零 reward
      导致 GRPO 无梯度信号。GiGPO 通过 anchor state 匹配同一状态下的不同
      action, 提供 step-level credit assignment。
      改动量 ~250 LOC, 零额外 GPU 成本 (critic-free)。
      从 verl-agent 官方实现移植 4 个核心函数到 RAGEN core_algos.py。
      anchor_obs 全链路已在 codebase 中采集 (env.py → es_manager → ctx_manager)。
      论文数据: Qwen2.5-1.5B ALFWorld GRPO 72.8% → GiGPO 86.1% (+13.3pp)。
      如 exp027 step 10 早停触发 (success ≤12%), 立即启动 exp028_gigpo。
    hypothesis: >
      GiGPO step-level credit 解决 sparse reward 梯度消失, 突破 10% plateau,
      达 success ≥30% (weak pass) 或 ≥50% (strong pass)。
    metrics: ["success_rate", "action_is_valid", "kl_divergence", "entropy", "step_group_avg_size", "step_advantage_magnitude"]
    gpu_hours_estimate: 84
    framing_ref: "reviewer_concern_1"
    nine_dim: [1, 4]

  - plan_id: "plan_003"
    title: "Multi-seed baseline replication (3 seeds)"
    claim: "Claim 1"
    phase: "A"
    priority: "P1"
    depends_on: ["plan_002"]
    registry_id: null
    status: "planned"
    description: >
      Replicate best Phase A config across 3 random seeds to report
      mean ± std success rate. Required for statistical credibility
      of all downstream comparisons.
    hypothesis: >
      Baseline success rate is reproducible (std < 5pp across seeds).
    metrics: ["success_rate_mean", "success_rate_std"]
    gpu_hours_estimate: 252
    framing_ref: null
    nine_dim: [3]

  # ============================================================
  # Phase B: B-IAVR Selective Verification
  # ============================================================

  - plan_id: "plan_004"
    title: "Action-change reward signal analysis"
    claim: "Claim 2"
    phase: "B"
    priority: "P0"
    depends_on: ["plan_001"]
    registry_id: null
    status: "planned"
    description: >
      Before training B-IAVR policy, collect action-change statistics from
      Phase A always-on runs: (1) what fraction of verifications trigger
      action change, (2) correlation between action change and episode
      success, (3) per-task-type breakdown. This informs reward design
      and provides empirical grounding for Claim 2.
    hypothesis: >
      Action change after verification positively correlates with episode
      success (r > 0.2), and most verifications are confirmatory (>60%
      produce no action change).
    metrics: ["action_change_rate", "action_change_success_correlation", "confirmatory_rate"]
    gpu_hours_estimate: 4
    framing_ref: "reviewer_concern_3"
    nine_dim: [1, 4]

  - plan_id: "plan_005"
    title: "B-IAVR binary verify/skip policy (GRPO)"
    claim: "Claim 1"
    phase: "B"
    priority: "P0"
    depends_on: ["plan_002", "plan_004"]
    registry_id: null
    status: "planned"
    description: >
      Train selective verification policy via GRPO. Agent learns a binary
      decision (verify / skip) at each step. Reward = task_success +
      alpha * action_change_when_verified - beta * verification_cost.
      Initialize from Phase A best checkpoint. Action-change component
      encourages verification only when it would change the agent's action.
    hypothesis: >
      B-IAVR achieves verification rate ↓40%+ compared to always-on
      while maintaining success within 5pp of baseline.
    metrics: ["success_rate", "verification_rate", "cost_reduction", "action_change_rate"]
    gpu_hours_estimate: 168
    framing_ref: "reviewer_concern_1"
    nine_dim: [1, 4]

  - plan_id: "plan_006"
    title: "B-IAVR multi-seed replication (3 seeds)"
    claim: "Claim 1"
    phase: "B"
    priority: "P1"
    depends_on: ["plan_005"]
    registry_id: null
    status: "planned"
    description: >
      Replicate best B-IAVR config across 3 seeds. Report mean ± std for
      success rate, verification rate, and cost reduction.
    hypothesis: >
      B-IAVR cost reduction is reproducible (std < 5pp across seeds).
    metrics: ["success_rate_mean", "success_rate_std", "verification_rate_mean", "cost_reduction_mean"]
    gpu_hours_estimate: 252
    framing_ref: null
    nine_dim: [3]

  # ============================================================
  # Phase C: Ablation Matrix & Causal Analysis
  # ============================================================

  - plan_id: "plan_007"
    title: "No-verify ablation"
    claim: "Claim 3"
    phase: "C"
    priority: "P0"
    depends_on: ["plan_002"]
    registry_id: null
    status: "planned"
    description: >
      Train agent with verification completely disabled. Same GRPO config
      as Phase A but no self-verification step. Lower bound for ablation
      matrix — demonstrates verification value.
    hypothesis: >
      Removing verification drops success by ≥10pp vs always-on baseline,
      confirming verification contributes to task performance.
    metrics: ["success_rate", "action_is_valid"]
    gpu_hours_estimate: 84
    framing_ref: null
    nine_dim: [4]

  - plan_id: "plan_008"
    title: "Random-p verification ablation (p=0.3, 0.5, 0.7)"
    claim: "Claim 3"
    phase: "C"
    priority: "P0"
    depends_on: ["plan_002"]
    registry_id: null
    status: "planned"
    description: >
      Verify at random with probability p ∈ {0.3, 0.5, 0.7}. No learning —
      just stochastic verification on top of Phase A checkpoint. Heuristic
      baseline for Claim 3 (learned > heuristic).
    hypothesis: >
      Random verification underperforms B-IAVR at same verification budget:
      either lower success or higher verification rate for same success.
    metrics: ["success_rate", "verification_rate", "cost_reduction"]
    gpu_hours_estimate: 6
    framing_ref: null
    nine_dim: [2, 4]

  - plan_id: "plan_009"
    title: "Confidence-threshold verification ablation"
    claim: "Claim 3"
    phase: "C"
    priority: "P0"
    depends_on: ["plan_002"]
    registry_id: null
    status: "planned"
    description: >
      Verify only when model's next-token entropy exceeds threshold τ.
      Sweep τ ∈ {0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0}. Heuristic baseline representing
      "verify when uncertain" strategy.
    hypothesis: >
      Confidence-threshold achieves some cost reduction but is suboptimal
      vs learned B-IAVR policy because entropy doesn't capture verification
      informativeness.
    metrics: ["success_rate", "verification_rate", "cost_reduction"]
    gpu_hours_estimate: 8
    framing_ref: null
    nine_dim: [2, 4]

  - plan_id: "plan_010"
    title: "Entropy-controlled action-change analysis"
    claim: "Claim 2"
    phase: "C"
    priority: "P0"
    depends_on: ["plan_004"]
    registry_id: null
    status: "planned"
    description: >

    hypothesis: >
      Partial correlation between action change and success remains

    metrics: ["partial_correlation", "p_value", "per_stratum_effect_size"]
    gpu_hours_estimate: 4
    framing_ref: "reviewer_concern_3"
    nine_dim: [4]

    phase: "C"
    priority: "P0"
    depends_on: ["plan_002"]
    registry_id: null

    phase: "C"
    priority: "P1"
    depends_on: ["plan_005"]
    registry_id: null
    status: "planned"
    description: >

    metrics: ["success_rate", "verification_rate", "cost_reduction", "training_convergence_step"]
    gpu_hours_estimate: 336
    framing_ref: "reviewer_concern_3"

    title: "Verification cost weight sensitivity (alpha/beta sweep)"

    registry_id: null
    status: "planned"

      Sweep alpha (action-change weight) and beta (verification cost

    gpu_hours_estimate: 120
    framing_ref: null
    nine_dim: [5]
